title: How heatwaves impact people with disabilities
description:
Heatwaves are uncomfortable for everyone. But people living with disabilities face additional and specific challenges that can compromise their health and well-being. Many of these issues - from struggling service dogs to overheating wheelchairs - are frequently overlooked, even in public advice and emergency planning.

Maddie Molloy is a BBC climate and science reporter who is also profoundly deaf. She explains some of the challenges a heatwave can pose for deaf people, the visually impaired and people who use wheelchairs. We also hear from Blessing Odukoya, Emily Davison, Maddie Haining and Osayuki Igbinoba about how they cope with the heat.

summaryZh: 本集由 Hannah Gelbart 主持，探討熱浪如何對身心障礙者造成額外且常被忽略的影響。BBC 氣候與科學記者 Maddie（她為重度聽損）與她的助聽犬 Cole 分享個人經驗；節目亦訪問輪椅使用者（含一位 18 歲倡議者）、雙腿截肢者 Osa Yuki、作家 Blessing Olukoya、導盲犬使用者 Emily Davison 等人。來賓描述的問題包括：輪椅座墊悶熱、金屬與黑色部位過燙導致難以推行與皮膚破損或褥瘡、義肢內襯悶熱引發熱疹、輔具與電池（輪椅電池、人工耳蝸等）在高溫下故障、輔助動物中暑，以及因無空調或電梯故障而被困的交通阻礙。受訪者呼籲更具包容性的防疫與應變規劃（例如可及的交通、備援充電與更多現場協助），並分享實用應對法：多補水、放慢活動節奏、利用輪椅杯架放水瓶、注意輔助動物與裝置的防暑保護。
summaryEn: Presenter Hannah Gelbart examines how heatwaves add specific, often overlooked risks for people with disabilities. BBC climate and science reporter Maddie, who is profoundly deaf and has a hearing dog Cole, and interviewees including wheelchair users, a double-above-knee amputee Osa Yuki, writer Blessing Olukoya and guide-dog owner Emily Davison describe problems such as sweaty, poorly ventilated wheelchair seats that cause skin irritation and pressure sores, hot metal and drained wheelchair batteries, overheating prosthetic liners and heat rash, failures of assistive technology (including cochlear implants), stressed assistance animals, and being stranded by non‑air‑conditioned or inaccessible transport and broken lifts. Guests call for more inclusive guidance and emergency planning (accessible transport, backup charging and staffing), and share practical tips: stay hydrated, slow down, keep water bottles handy (use wheelchair cup holders), and protect assistance animals and devices.
